reasons: First PromQL line uses a fixed range [5m] instead of [$__rate_interval], which the hard rules forbid; the two formulas also use different ranges.

The $host template variable (tag prefix host, default *) should become a host label matcher, e.g. host_name=~"$host" if that label is observed in the dataset, but neither query includes it, so the series set differs from the Datadog request.

The candidate wraps redis.cpu.time (a monotonic sum in seconds) in rate(), yielding cores of CPU use. Datadog redis.cpu.sys/user are queried as plain avg values, so the quantity is only the same if those Datadog metrics are themselves cumulative CPU-seconds; this needs confirming before translating.
The state label is catalogued but not in the observed dataset labels, so the state matcher's label name is unverified against the target dataset.
